introduction_and_tips.title: Fueling for Success
introduction_and_tips.content: Knowing what to eat, and when to eat can be a challenge. As a college student, it’s hard to find the time to make food, let alone look for recipes. This cookbook was put together by USU senior dietetic students for students. We hope that whether you are part of an athletic team or just hitting the gym to improve your health, that you find something that helps you perform your best and fuels you for success!

macronutrients.definition: Food is composed of macronutrients and micronutrients. Macronutrients, often referred to as macros, are carbohydrates, protein, and fat. Micronutrients are vitamins and minerals, but we won’t talk much about them here.
macronutrients.carbohydrates: Carbohydrates, are the body’s main source of fuel. Because of this, diets low in carbohydrates leave people feeling tired and not able to physically perform as well in the gym, on the court, or on the field. Simple carbs, such as refined grains and sugar, release energy very quickly. Whole grains and fruit contain more complex carbs and are also a better source of fiber, vitamins, and minerals. They don’t release energy as quickly, meaning they provide a more steady, sustained source of fuel.
macronutrients.protein: Protein is the building block of muscle and important to every aspect of our body’s function. Athletes typically focus on protein and try to get as much as they can, but be aware that you don’t need as much protein as you do carbohydrates. Your body has a threshold and can only absorb about 20-40 grams of protein, depending on the person, in one sitting.
macronutrients.fat: Fat plays a role in the absorption of certain vitamins and hormone production. When exercise lasts for a long time, the body will switch over to fat as its energy source. It takes the longest to digest out of the three macronutrients, so it’s best not to have a lot of it before a workout. Aim to get your fats from healthy sources like nuts, seeds, avocados, and vegetable oils.

introduction_and_tips.hydration: Hydration is an important part of an athlete’s health and performance. Dehydration not only leads to decreased energy and performance, but it can be dangerous. Drink consistently throughout the day and even more when you are working out or competing. Pay attention to the color of your urine--the lighter the better--and how much you are sweating! It’s better to maintain hydration than to become dehydrated and try to rehydrate. Avoid using sports drinks unless your workout/competition is longer than 90 minutes, you sweat heavily or are in the heat.
introduction_and_tips.pre_workout_fuel: When your body has the right fuel, you will be able to work out longer and harder! Although everyone is different, a good rule is to have a meal 3-4 hours and a snack 1-2 hours before a workout or competition. A pre-workout meal should be high in carbohydrates and low in protein. Fiber and fat tend to make a meal harder to digest, so try to keep these to a minimum or at least a few hours before an intense workout. A snack before physical activity should be made up of mostly simple carbohydrates and little protein, fat, and fiber. More importantly, listen to your body and learn to recognize when it’s likes to be fueled.
introduction_and_tips.post_workout_recovery: Emphasis is often put on a “window of time” when a snack or meal should be eaten after a workout but according to more current research the stress over timing is not needed. Instead focus on having good meals and snacks throughout the day to keep you energized as you go. As mentioned previously, carbohydrates are the body’s preferred source of energy and the carbohydrates you had eaten before and stored as glycogen, are likely gone after an intense workout. To best help you recover, eat something with carbohydrates and combine it with protein in a ratio of 3:1 (or 2:1). An example might be 60 gram of carbs with 20 grams of protein. Protein will aid in recovery to rebuild the tears in your muscles that may have occurred, making them stronger and ready for the next workout. The Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics recommend that “athletes eat anywhere from 1.2 to 2 grams of protein [depending on activity] per kilogram of body weight per day. Although many athletes use shakes and supplements as part of their daily protein intake, whole foods generally provide better overall nutrition and should be a first choice when possible.”

recipes.name: Mango Smoothie
recipes.description: Smoothies are an amazing "go to" snack! Add a splash of orange juice to this one for an extra tropical flavor! Did you know that one cup of diced mango has 100% of your daily need for vitamin C, 35% of vitamin A and 20% of an important B vitamin called folate?
ingredients: 1 banana (if frozen leave out some ice)
directions: Combine ingredients in blender, blend to desired consistency

recipes.name: Choco Peanut Butter Power Smoothie
recipes.description: This delicious combination of flavors is a great way to start the day, have on hand as a power snack or end the day with a yummy, healthy treat! Using plain Greek yogurt adds extra protein and helps bring out the chocolate flavor!
ingredients: 1 Tbsp. peanut butter (or other nut butter)
directions: Combine ingredients in blender, blend to desired consistency

recipes.name: Strawberry Banana Smoothie
recipes.description: Bananas are such a valuable ingredient. They are the secret to a sweet, creamy and nutritious smoothie. Go bananas for this classic combo of strawberry and banana!
optional_ingredients: 1 cup Greek yogurt (for a post workout smoothie)
directions: Combine ingredients in blender, blend to desired consistency

recipes.name: Piña Colada
recipes.description: Everyday can feel like a tropical paradise with this scrumptious smoothie! Great for a pre workout snack, make it a post workout snack by adding greek yogurt or a protein powder.
optional_ingredients: 1 cup Greek yogurt (for post workout smoothie)
directions: Combine ingredients in blender, blend to desired consistency

recipes.name: Green Island Getaway
recipes.description: For an extra sweet flavor use a frozen, ripe banana. Ripe bananas are perfect for smoothies, so don't throw them out. To make it easier for later use, peel bananas before freezing them in a freezer safe storage bag.
directions: Combine ingredients in blender, blend to desired consistency

recipes.name: Cherry Chia Bites
recipes.description: Chia seeds were a staple food for the ancient Aztec people of Central America. The word "chia" directly translates to STRENGTH!! Let these small, beautiful bites fuel your workouts!
directions: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl
Refrigerate for 1 hour or freeze for 15 minutes
Form into 20 one-inch balls

recipes.name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Bites
recipes.description: The perfect combo! Chocolate and peanut butter matched with flaxseed is a great tasting energy bite that is a great source of protein, fiber and healthy fats! What else can you ask for?
directions: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl
Refrigerate for 1 hour or freeze for 15 minutes
Form into 20 one-inch balls

recipes.name: Lemon Blueberry Bites
recipes.description: Refreshing and sweet! Lemons are a great source of vitamin C which supports the immune system and enhances the bodies absorption of iron! With these bites you can pump the iron and know that your body is absorbing it too!
directions: Blend almonds, lemon juice and honey
Add half of the oats and blend until smooth
Stir in remaining unblended oats, chia seeds and blueberries
Refrigerate for one hour or freeze for 15 minutes
Form into 24 one-inch balls

recipes.name: Apple Cinnamon Bites
recipes.description: Apple Pie Spice is a store-bought mixture of ginger, nutmeg, cinnamon, allspice, ginger and cloves. If you don't have this mixture on hand feel free to add a small dash of each of those spices or just the ones you have on hand! Spice it up!
directions: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl
Refrigerate for 1 hour or freeze for 15 minutes
Form into 16 one-inch balls

recipes.name: Pumpkin Bites
recipes.description: Don't wait for the Fall to try these lovely bites. The health benefits of cinnamon, cloves, ginger and nutmeg include reducing inflammation and aiding in digestion.
directions: Mix all the ingredients in a bowl
Refrigerate for 1 hour or freeze for 15 minutes
Form into 14 one-inch balls

recipes.name: Peanut Butter Trail Mix
recipes.description: Peanut butter is a college student's best friend! Use whatever type of chocolate chip floats your boat, whether it's milk, semi-sweet, or dark.
directions: Mix all the ingredients together
Store in a sealed bag or mason jar

recipes.name: Savory Seed Mix
recipes.description: If you're looking for a savory flavor that packs a spicy kick this savory seed mix is for you! The seeds in this recipe are a great source of protein, fiber, B vitamins and vitamin E. For a less spicy mix cut back on the cayenne pepper.
directions: Mix all ingredients together
Store in a sealed bag or mason jar

recipes.name: The Cereal Lover Mix
recipes.description: The perfect mix of crunchy and sweet! Use your favorite cereal or switch out the dried fruit for another yummy option. This is a perfect energy on the go and a great pre workout snack option.
directions: Mix all the ingredients together
Store in a sealed bag or mason jar

recipes.name: Avocado Toast
recipes.description: The iconic avocado toast! Avocados are an awesome source of healthy fats to help keep you full and give you energy; however, a higher fat meal isn’t ideal before a workout. Consider having this one post-workout with one of the sources of added protein listed below.
directions: Slice avocado in half lengthwise. Cut one of the halves lengthwise into 4 or 5 thin slices. You can store the other half of the avocado for later by squeezing some lime over it and sticking it in the fridge.
Toast a slice of whole grain bread.
Lay avocado slices across whole grain bread, squeeze some lime over the top, and give it a dash of salt and pepper.
To make this recipe good for post-workout, it needs a good protein source. You can top it with an egg (any style), cottage cheese, or pumpkin seeds.

recipes.name: Banana PB Wrap
recipes.description: This is another quick grab and go post workout snack. This is a good example of how easy a workout snack can be. Grab a food that contains carbohydrates and add some protein!
directions: Spread peanut butter on tortilla
Arrange banana slices on peanut butter and sprinkle with chia seeds
Roll into a wrap and enjoy.

recipes.name: Meat and Cheese Wrap
recipes.description: This wrap, combined with a cold glass of chocolate milk or some fruit, makes a great post-workout meal. Make several of these at the beginning of the week and eat them for the next 3 or 4 days. They’re perfect for an on-the-go day!
directions: Spread cream cheese on tortilla
Place sliced turkey and shredded cheese on cream cheese
Slice cherry tomatoes in half top wrap with them, add spinach
Roll into a wrap and enjoy

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Wrap
recipes.description: Here’s another fun post-workout meal where you can make several in advance and take them on the go. Make sure to have it with some chocolate milk or fruit to meet a 2:1 ratio of carbs to protein.
directions: Mix shredded chicken with barbecue sauce. Spread on tortilla.
Sprinkle cheese and onion on top of chicken.
Slice cherry tomatoes in half and sprinkle on chicken. Add romaine lettuce.
Start to roll the wrap from the edge. When you’re halfway, fold the ends down, and continue to roll.
Combine Greek yogurt with ranch mix. Serve as dipping sauce for the wrap.

recipes.name: Power Packed Oatmeal
recipes.description: Oats are a great whole grain. Whole grains act as complex carbs that can help you feel full longer. For less thick oatmeal add more milk. For more power packing, feel free to add nuts, flax seed or chia seeds.
directions: In a small pot, heat oats, 1/2 cup almond milk, 1/3 cup water, strawberries, honey, vanilla, and salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until mixture is thick and oats are plump, 5 to 7 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Mix it with yogurt to cool.
Top oatmeal with peanut butter.

recipes.name: Fantastic Fruit Dip
recipes.description: Apples are the second most consumed fruit in the United States. This fruit is known for having a good source of dietary fiber and vitamin C with the peel included so don’t toss it out. Approximately, each medium sized apple gives 4.4 grams of fiber.
directions: Cut apple into slices. Mix peanut butter and yogurt together in small bowl. Dip apple slices into dip and enjoy.

nutrition.servings_and_size: 1 medium apple with approx ½ cup dip

recipes.name: Chicken Salad
recipes.description: To make it easy, you can buy the precooked frozen diced chicken in most stores. This is also another one of those recipes that plain Greek yogurt works better than vanilla.
directions: Stir the yogurt and cranberry sauce together in a mixing bowl.
Add all the other ingredients. Stir until the cranberry yogurt mix is evenly distributed.
Either spread between two slices of bread or pita to make a sandwich, or eat as is with crackers or a spoon. Pack individuals servings into containers and refrigerate.

recipes.name: Turkey Stacks
recipes.description: The apple is both a fun, sweet twist and nutritious. You can trade out the cheddar cheese for another favorite like pepper jack or colby. To make this a good post-workout snack, add a serving of fruit or a glass of chocolate milk!
ingredients: 5 thin slices cheddar cheese (size of the cracker, about ¼” thick)
directions: If using mustard, place a dot on each cracker.
Fold turkey slices in four and place on top of cracker.
Top turkey with cheddar and apple slices.

recipes.name: Egg-cellent Snack Muffins
recipes.description: This recipe is versatile in that you can switch out the ham and vegetables for different breakfast meats and vegetables. Eggs are packed with protein and other nutrients. Make a batch of twelve and eat them throughout the week.
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F.
Spray a 12-cup muffin pan with non-stick cooking spray (the better you spray, the less it will stick!) or use thick muffin liners.
In a large mixing bowl, beat eggs. Add in remaining ingredients and mix together.
Scoop 1/3 cup of mixture into each muffin liner. Bake for 20-25 minutes or until the center of the muffin is completely cooked.

nutrition.note: Have one snack muffin with a slice of toast to make it a 2:1 carb to protein post-workout snack.

recipes.name: Quick Breakfast Sandwich
recipes.description: Who says breakfast can only be in the morning? This sandwich makes a great post workout snack with the protein you need to refuel and get ready for the next time you hit the gym, field, or wherever you like to move. For more protein you can add a slice of turkey or for more flavor add a fresh tomato.
ingredients: 1 large fried egg (or scrambled if preferred)
directions: Slice and toast bagels, if desired. Spread cream cheese on bagels.
Fry or scramble one large egg.
Place egg, spinach and avocado on one side of the bagel and sandwich between the two slices. Enjoy.

recipes.name: Banana Pancake
recipes.description: Great post workout snack! Serve with your favorite peanut or nut butter and a cup of chocolate or regular milk to make a better combination of carbohydrate and protein. If you do not have oats on hand, 2 tablespoons of flour will work as well. For fluffier pancakes, add 1 tsp of baking powder.
directions: Mash bananas in a large bowl until smooth. Mix in eggs and vanilla until well combined, then mix in oats and cinnamon.

Heat a skillet to medium and add in a scoop* of the pancake batter. Smooth out to form an even layer. Cook for about 2-3 minutes until you start to see bubbles releasing from the top of the batter. Flip and cook until the other side is golden brown, about 1-2 minutes.
Garnish with peanut butter or your favorite nut butter.

nutrition.note: * Use 1/2 cup for scooping batter to yield 4 thicker pancakes, use 1/3 cup to yield 6 smaller pancakes.

recipes.name: Killer Quesadilla
recipes.description: This isn’t your classic cheese quesadilla. Chopped chicken adds more protein, and pico de gallo gives it a great flavor and texture! If you’re afraid of cooking chicken, you can always find pre-cooked chicken in the lunch meat aisle or in the frozen meat section.
ingredients: 2 Tbsp. pico de gallo (or salsa of choice)
directions: Mix together chicken, cheese, pico de gallo, and chopped green bell pepper.
Place tortilla in a pan on low to medium heat and spread chicken and cheese mixture over one half. Fold the tortilla in half.
Heat tortilla until browned on one side and cheese starts to melt (about 1-2 minutes). Flip and brown the other side (about 1-2 minutes).
Mix Greek yogurt and ranch mix together. Serve with the quesadilla.

recipes.name: Banana Popsicle
recipes.description: The perfect treat on a hot summer day, or any day you want to feel like your in a tropical paradise. The perfect post-workout snack or post workout dessert!
directions: Cut each banana in half and insert the bottom of each with a wooden popsicle stick, about 1/3 of the way into banana.
Place bananas on a parchment paper lined baking sheet.
Freeze bananas 30 minutes.

Place the vanilla yogurt in a tall pint glass and carefully dip each partially frozen banana into the yogurt to coat leaving 1/2 inch at the bottom uncoated with yogurt. Line yogurt-coated bananas back on the parchment paper and freeze until firm, about 1 hour.

Next, microwave the peanut butter until smooth and creamy, about 30-45 seconds. Drizzle peanut butter evenly over frozen yogurt coated bananas then place on the baking sheet to freeze once last time. Freeze until peanut butter is firm, about 30 minutes.
Enjoy immediately or wrap each banana in plastic wrap and store in freezer for up to 3 months.

recipes.name: Citrus Chicken Pasta Salad
recipes.description: This pasta salad is another great dish you can make and keep in the fridge for a few days. It’s a great post-workout meal, and you can pair it with some fruit or another carbohydrate to bring it up to that 2:1 ratio. If no blender is available, shake dressing ingredients together in a mason jar.
directions: Cook the pasta according to package direction. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Place the cooled pasta in a large bowl. Add in the spinach and the halved cherry tomatoes.
Add chicken to salad and toss to combine.
Sprinkle almonds and feta cheese over the salad.

For the dressing: combine all of the ingredients together except for the oil in a blender. Blend until all ingredients are well incorporated. Slowly add in the oil in a steady stream and pulse until combined.
Toss the salad with the dressing (to taste; you may not want/need all of it) and enjoy. ONLY toss what you plan on eating as the dressing makes the spinach "soggy" for leftovers.

recipes.name: Tuna Sandwich
recipes.description: Tuna is a good nutritious, budget-friendly protein to make a regular part in your diet! Greek yogurt replaces the mayonnaise in this sandwich to give it more protein. Carrots and celery give it a great texture and color.
directions: Mix together tuna, Greek yogurt, celery, carrot, and lemon pepper.
Toast two slices of bread.
Spread half of the mixture onto the bread and sandwich together

recipes.name: Simply Parfait
recipes.description: When looking for a whole wheat cereal use the ingredient label. Look for cereal that says “whole grain” as the first ingredient. Enjoy this simple recipe with a variety of fruits and nuts.
ingredients: 1 cup Greek yogurt (your choice of flavor)
directions: Layer 1/4 cup of cereal in a glass or mason jar
Add 2 1/2 tablespoons of the yogurt
Add a few strawberry slices
Sprinkle some peanuts
Repeat the process and finish with a layer of strawberries

recipes.name: High-Protein Egg & Veggie Muffins
recipes.description: A fantastic meal-prep snack filled with protein from fresh eggs and dietary fiber from vibrant local vegetables. Pair with a slice of whole-wheat toast for the perfect post-workout recovery carb-to-protein ratio.
ingredients: 1/4 cup red bell pepper, finely diced
1/4 cup fresh mushrooms or carrots, diced
1 cup grated Paneer (or local Amul shredded cheese)
1/2 cup fresh baby spinach (Palak), finely shredded
directions: Preheat oven to 180 degrees C (350 degrees F).
Grease a 12-cup muffin pan thoroughly with a non-stick oil spray or ghee so they don't stick.
In a large mixing bowl, whisk the eggs well. Whisk in the diced vegetables, paneer, and a pinch of salt and pepper.
Scoop 1/3 cup of the mixture into each muffin slot. Bake for 20-25 minutes until the centers are completely set.

nutrition.note: Have one savory snack muffin with a slice of whole-wheat toast to reach an optimal post-workout carb-to-protein recovery combo.

recipes.name: Quick Breakfast Sandwich
recipes.description: Who says breakfast food is only for the morning? This sandwich is powered by fresh eggs, spinach, and healthy fats. To boost the protein even further, you can add a slice of grilled chicken breast or grilled paneer instead of western deli cold-cuts.
ingredients: 1 whole-wheat bun or multi-grain bagel, sliced in half
1 large egg (fried or scrambled as per preference)
Small handful of fresh spinach (Palak) leaves
2 tsp. garlic-herb cheese spread or soft paneer spread
2-4 thin slices of ripe avocado or fresh tomato
directions: Slice and lightly toast the bun on a tawa. Spread the garlic cheese spread evenly on both sides.
Cook one large egg on the tawa using a drop of oil or ghee.
Layer the cooked egg, fresh spinach, and avocado/tomato slices between the bun halves. Enjoy fresh.

recipes.name: Desi Banana Oats Pancake
recipes.description: An excellent vegetarian post-workout recovery snack! Serve with a tablespoon of peanut butter and a glass of milk to hit your ideal protein targets. If you do not have oats, regular whole wheat flour (atta) works perfectly too.
ingredients: 2 eggs (or substitute with 1/4 cup milk + 1 tbsp ground flaxseeds for eggless)
1/2 cup quick-cook rolled oats (or whole wheat atta)
directions: Mash the bananas in a bowl until completely smooth. Whisk in the eggs and vanilla, then stir in the oats and cinnamon.
Heat a non-stick pan or tawa over medium heat and pour a small ladle of the batter. Smooth it into an even circle.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until bubbles form on top, flip gently, and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes until golden brown.
Garnish with a dollop of peanut butter or local honey.

nutrition.note: Use a 1/2 cup scoop for 4 thick pancakes, or a 1/3 cup scoop to yield 6 smaller, thinner pancakes.

recipes.name: Spiced Paneer & Chicken Quesadilla
recipes.description: A protein-packed wrap that replaces processed meats with fresh shredded chicken breast or pan-seared paneer cubes. Accompanied by a refreshing high-protein dip made from fresh thick Indian curd.
ingredients: 4 Tbsp. finely chopped boiled chicken breast (or crumbled paneer)
2 Tbsp. fresh kachumber salad (diced onions, tomatoes, coriander)

extra_components.name: High-Protein Herb Dip
ingredients: 2 Tbsp. thick hung curd (Greek yogurt style)
1/2 tsp. chaat masala, roasted cumin powder, and mint leaves

directions: In a small bowl, mix together the chicken/paneer, cheese, capsicum, and kachumber salad.
Place a chapati on a tawa over low-medium heat. Spread the mixture evenly over one half and fold it over.
Press down gently and toast until golden-brown and the cheese starts melting (1-2 minutes per side).
Whisk the hung curd with the spices and mint. Slice the quesadilla and serve warm alongside the dip.

recipes.name: Mango Berry Yogurt Popsicles
recipes.description: The perfect cooling treat after a intense workout in hot weather. Packed with calcium and high protein from thick local dahi/yogurt and naturally sweetened with seasonal fresh fruits like mangoes or bananas.
ingredients: 2 large ripe bananas or 1 cup sweet mango pulp
2 cups thick vanilla or plain dahi (Greek-style curd)
directions: If using bananas, peel and cut them in half, then insert a wooden stick 1/3 of the way into each piece.
Place them on a plate lined with butter paper and freeze for 30 minutes.
Pour the thick curd into a tall glass. Dip each chilled fruit piece directly into the curd to coat it evenly, leaving a little space near the stick. Return to the freezer for 1 hour.
Gently warm the peanut butter in a small bowl until fluid. Drizzle it over the frozen yogurt-coated fruit, and freeze for another 30 minutes until set.

recipes.name: Indian Fish & Pasta Salad
recipes.description: This refreshing cold salad swaps out western tuna cans for freshly steamed or pan-seared local fish (like Kingfish/Surmai or Rohu/Katla, deboned and flaked) or paneer cubes. It keeps incredibly well in the fridge for simple meal prep.
ingredients: 1 cup cooked, flaked local white fish (Surmai/Rohu) or paneer cubes
1 cup fresh baby spinach or chopped lettuce
1 cup cherry tomatoes, cut into halves
1/3 cup crumbled paneer or feta cheese
1/3 cup slivered almonds or roasted peanuts

extra_components.name: Zesty Citrus Dressing
ingredients: 1 tsp. ginger-garlic paste or mustard paste
1/4 cup olive oil or cold-pressed mustard oil

directions: Boil the pasta according to package instructions until al dente. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Transfer the cooled pasta to a large bowl. Toss gently with the spinach, tomatoes, and flaked fish (or paneer).
Garnish the top with the almonds/peanuts and crumbled paneer.
To make the dressing: Whisk the juices, honey, spices, and oil together in a small jar until fully emulsified.
Drizzle the dressing over the salad right before eating so the greens stay crisp.

recipes.name: High-Protein Local Fish Sandwich
recipes.description: A budget-friendly, highly nutritious sandwich utilizing freshly cooked local fish fillets or protein-rich crumbled paneer. Fresh thick curd replaces heavy mayonnaise to maximize the protein and keep it light.
ingredients: 2 slices multi-grain or whole-wheat sandwich bread
1 cup cooked, mashed deboned fish (or 1 cup mashed paneer/tofu)
2 Tbsp. finely chopped cucumber or celery
1 tsp. lemon juice and black pepper powder
directions: In a bowl, combine your mashed fish or paneer with the thick curd, cucumber, carrot, lemon juice, and black pepper.
Toast your two slices of whole-wheat bread on a tawa until crispy.
Spread the mint chutney lightly on the bread, layer the filling generously, close the sandwich, and slice.

recipes.name: Anar & Strawberry Curd Parfait
recipes.description: A beautifully layered, calcium-rich recipe featuring seasonal Indian fruits like pomegranate (anar) and bananas, paired with high-fiber whole grain cereals and rich curd.
ingredients: 1/2 cup fresh pomegranate pearls (anar) or sliced strawberries
3/4 cup high-fiber muesli or crushed whole-wheat flakes
1 cup thick set curd (dahi or sweet mishti doi alternative)
directions: Take a clean serving glass or small mason jar and drop 1/4 cup of the cereal at the bottom.
Spoon 2-3 tablespoons of thick curd directly over the cereal layer.
Drop a generous layer of pomegranate pearls and sliced fruits over the curd, followed by a sprinkle of nuts.
Repeat the layers once more, finishing with vibrant fruit and nuts on the top. Serve chilled.

recipes.name: Almond & Date Power Bites
recipes.description: A natural, sugar-free energy burst perfect for an active Indian lifestyle. This mix combines iron-rich dates with brain-boosting almonds to give you a clean, non-heavy fuel source right before your yoga session or gym workout.
directions: Pulse the almonds and flaxseeds in a mixer until coarsely chopped.
Add the pitted dates and cardamom powder, then pulse until the mixture binds together like a dough.
Form into 10 even, one-inch balls and consume immediately or store in an airtight container.

recipes.name: Spicy Paneer Bhurji
recipes.description: The perfect post-workout vegetarian muscle recovery meal. Fresh Indian cottage cheese (Paneer) provides high-quality, bioavailable dairy protein to repair worn-out muscle tissues quickly.
directions: Heat oil in a pan and splutter the cumin seeds.
Saute the chopped onions and green chilies for 2 minutes until translucent.
Add tomatoes and turmeric powder, cooking until soft.
Crumble the paneer directly into the pan, season with salt, and toss well for 2 to 3 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coriander leaves and serve warm.

recipes.name: Sattu Hydration Fuel
recipes.description: Known as the original Indian powerhouse drink, roasted chana sattu provides sustained energy and cools down the body system. Ideal as a light, non-bloating pre-workout drink.
directions: Add sattu to a shaker or a deep jug.
Pour in cold water slowly while whisking continuously to prevent lumps.
Stir in the lemon juice, black salt, and roasted cumin powder.
Drop in torn mint leaves, stir well, and drink fresh.

recipes.name: Oats & Moong Dal Cheela
recipes.description: A complex carbohydrate and plant-based protein powerhouse designed to replenish your body's glycogen reserves after an intense gym session.
ingredients: 1/2 cup instant oats, ground into flour
4 Tbsp. yellow moong dal flour (or Besan)
directions: In a bowl, whisk oats flour, moong dal flour, curd, ginger, hing, and salt.
Gradually add water to form a smooth, pourable pancake batter consistency.
Fold in the chopped spinach leaves.
Pour a ladleful onto a hot, lightly greased non-stick tawa, spreading it into a thin circle.
Cook for 2 minutes on each side until crisp and golden brown.

recipes.name: Tangy Sprouts Chaat
recipes.description: A live-enzyme packed fitness snack. Steamed moong sprouts combine with crunch and tang to deliver clean vegetarian fiber, vitamins, and lean recovery macros.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups sprouted green moong dal, lightly steamed
directions: Steam the green moong sprouts for 3 to 5 minutes so they are cooked but still crunchy.
Transfer sprouts to a mixing bowl and let them cool down slightly.
Toss in the cucumber, tomato, and roasted peanuts.
Drizzle lemon juice and sprinkle chaat masala and salt.
Mix thoroughly and enjoy immediately as a refreshing recovery snack.
